MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, MARCH 1, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR EDLER at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR EDLER led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Edler, Scott, Carman, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang

  Staff Members Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, FEBRUARY 1, 2021.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 1, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL SUCH
  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200353; ADDRESS: 42 EMPTY SADDLE ROAD,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: MR. MATT SCHNEIDER, ARCHITECT; A
  request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-200354) for one and two-story
  additions to be constructed along the front, side and rear yards of a single-story residence
  with a detached garage. A Minor Deviation (MD-200355) is required to decrease the front
  yard area by less than 10% and for the encroachment of the proposed addition into the
  required front yard which does not project closer to the property line than the forwardmost
  building line.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that this item was continued to allow the applicant time to work
  with the neighbor at 44 Empty Saddle Road, to address privacy concerns. The applicant has
  eliminated the second story deck that is adjacent to the shared property line and replaced the
  bathroom with no windows facing the neighbor at 44 Empty Saddle Road. Staff did not find records
  for the denial of a previous proposed two-story project at this address. Associate Planner Thom
  provided a presentation on PA-200353 summarizing the staff report.

  Associate Planner Thom recommended that the Planning Commission approve PA-200353 with
  the conditions as outlined in the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT expressed his disappointment with seeing the bathroom in the rear of the
  property and a 25’ bonus room.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that he preferred the original design since the new design
PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021
   includes more wall and height.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Associate Planner Thom stated that
  staff does not have concerns with the front façade materials combination of siding and stone.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked for the ridge height of the principal second story roof.
  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that it is approximately 23 ½’.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that there are eight neighbors in opposition of this project due to mass
  and asked why staff is supportive of this project in this neighborhood. In addition, he expressed his
  concern with access during construction.

  A brief discussion ensued on access for work vehicles during construction. Associate Planner
  Thom stated that conditions could be added in order to mitigate access issues.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that some of the objections are based upon an understanding that
  there was a denial at 44 Empty Saddle Road. Staff found no records for a proposal of a second
  story addition at the property.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN expressed her concern with the scale and stated that the property
  across the street has a second story that is very subtle. She also asked how emergency vehicle
  access will be addressed.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that if there are additional access needs then this could be added
  as a condition. Staff can work with the applicant and the building department to identify access
  areas.

  Planning Manager Naughton added that the next item that will be presented, which has an
  intermediate turnaround, was a result of a subdivision action. This is reviewed by the Land
  Development Unit of Los Angeles County Fire who looks at these type of access requirements.
  Typically, this kind of review is not required unless there is a Conditional Use Permit, a subdivision
  action or something to that effect. However, once the project gets to the permitting stage, it will go
  to the engineering division for specific access requirements with LA County Fire; they will be
  looking at distance to fire hydrants and if there is not sufficient distance, then they may require a
  new fire hydrant, but there will probably not be a requirement for a turnaround if there is not some
  type of subdivision action.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG inquired about the height of the second story at 19 Empty Saddle
  Road, which was recently approved by the Planning Commission. Associate Planner Thom stated
  that it is 24’ 6”. A foot less than the highest point of this project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO inquired about the square footage of the property at 19 Empty Saddle
  Road. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that it is about 450 sq. ft. less than this project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if the mature trees will remain. Associate Planner Thom
  stated that she is not sure but hopes that they will remain.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked why the issue of neighborhood compatibility is not being looked at
  more closely since there are eight neighbors who believe that this project is not compatible with
  the neighborhood.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that some of the objections to this project were due to the false
  assumption that this project had been proposed previously and was denied. There were no records
  of a project at this address – neither denied or withdrawn.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that, in regards to maintaining the Ranch Style character, the
  project does comply; however, the concerns are with the square footage of the home. She further
  stated that large buildings can be designed to look less massive, this project is on a large lot and
  is set back at least 54 ft. from the street. The second story will step back approximately 6 ft. from
  the first floor wall. Staff does not believe that this is out of character from the neighborhood, which
  has a variety of home sizes.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the issue is the addition or that it is second story. Associate
  Planner Thom stated that the issue is the second story and that it is in a prominent position on the
  street.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he is not proposing that the second story is inappropriate, rather,
  that it is a massive second story. In addition, the second story add-on that replaced the balcony,
  seems unnecessary.

  Matt Schneider, Architect, stated that the intention, for the bathroom that was added, was to

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021
   maximize space in the bonus room; the bonus room is 25 ft. long, but only 13 ft. wide. The problem
  with making the second story more narrow is that there are two separate spaces on the second
  floor, which is separated by the vaulted ceiling in the great room. Mr. Schneider stated that he
  could understand that looking at it from the street, it may look massive, but looking at the floor plan
  the bulk of the addition is on the west side of the home and a small bonus room. There is not a lot
  of space to make the bonus room smaller. He also stated, that as far as he knows, the mature
  vegetation will remain and any ground covering will be replaced after construction.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked the width from the house to the property line on the driveway side. Mr.
  Schneider stated that it is 7.5 ft. and 10 ft. from the second story.

  William Garrett, 14 Empty Saddle Road, stated that the staff report that groups Empty Saddle
  Road, Tanglewood Lane and Shadow Lane is inappropriate. Tanglewood Lane and Shadow Lane
  are not part of Empty Saddle HOA. Mr. Garrett stated that Empty Saddle HOA consists of 53
  homes that are predominantly single-family homes, generally in the range of 3,000 – 4500 sq. ft.
  range. In Exhibit C, the staff report indicates that the home at 48 Empty Saddle Road is 6,333 sq.
  ft. and believes that this is an error. Mr. Garrett expressed his concern with the street appearance
  of this house and stated that it is massive and out of scale with the very narrow road that
  approaches the property. There are two-story homes in the neighborhood but none are as
  prominent and on such a narrow street. Mr. Garrett stated that he could not locate any plans
  submitted for a previous project at this address, but it is his understanding that the City would not
  consider proposals for second-story additions.

  Katherine Hawkins, 44 Empty Saddle Road, stated that the removal of the balcony and raising the
  height of the windows have reduced the impact that this project would have had to her privacy.
  She expressed her concern with the windows at the back of the house and stated that she was
  disappointed with the photos used in the presentation which were taken of the flags (silhouette)
  through the vegetation. She asked that the Planning Commission view photos that were taken from
  her front yard and patio, which clearly show the flags. Ms. Hawkins stated that the hedges that are
  in her front yard would not provide a screen once the new walls are constructed since they will
  protrude well above the hedges.

  Michael Hawkins, 44 Empty Saddle Road, stated that he spoke to the former owner of 42 Empty
  Saddle Road, Mr. Benowitz, who stated that in the 1990’s he was proposing to build a two-story
  home and during initial discussions with city staff, he was informed that it would not be favored and
  decided not to proceed. He stated that the more recent owners of 42 Empty Saddle, the Wagner’s,
  also applied and after speaking to the neighbors and city staff, decided not to proceed with the
  project. He also stated that the owners at 14 Empty Saddle had also proposed to build a two-story
  home in the early 2000s; after speaking with neighbors and city staff decided not to proceed and
  were also told that there was a 4,000 sq. ft. cap on homes in the neighborhood. Mr. Hawkins also
  mentioned several single-story home projects in the neighborhood and spoke about the single-
  story addition that they suggested to the applicant. Mr. Hawkins also expressed his concern with
  access for construction.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked Mr. Hawkins if the removal of the balcony and raising the height of
  the window has addressed the privacy concerns that were discussed at the last meeting. Mr.
  Hawkins stated that this does address the privacy concerns and appreciates the changes. Mr.
  Hawkins stated that you can still see into their property from the rear windows.

  COMMISSIONER YOO asked if any second story addition is a concern. Mr. Hawkins stated that
  the streets are narrow and the lots are very private and this would destroy that. He stated that he
  would like to see a single-story solution.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that as he looks at the pictures of the patio of the flagged area and
  the back façade of the plan as proposed, aside from the two raised windows in the bonus room,
  there are no windows on that side. The only window is a picture window with no deck. Mr. Hawkins
  stated that in the rear, those windows do overlook the lot. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the roof
  of the garage impedes most of the view.

  Mr. Schneider stated that the Hawkins suggestions for making this a single-story addition include
  moving a pool and the location of the existing garage. In addition, there are lot coverage issues
  since they are at 26% of the 30% lot coverage and is not a viable solution for the homeowners.

  Mr. Hawkins asked if a Variance could be granted for the lot coverage issues to extend to the front
  of the property.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked about the possibility of making the vaulted ceiling in the great
  room flat. Mr. Schneider stated that one of the highlights of the home is having the vaulted ceiling
  in the great room.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if he was open to changing the roof pitch to 3:12. Mr.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  3
MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021
   Schneider stated that 4:12 are typical with Ranch style, but could consider it.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that they have met the code and addressed the privacy
  concerns. He is in favor of approval of the project.

  COMMISSIONER YOO stated that Mr. Hawkins stated that the privacy concern has been
  addressed. In addition, since the 90’s, things have evolved and he cannot rely on a hearsay denial
  of a proposal for a second story as a basis for denial of this project. COMMISSIONER YOO stated
  that even though the concerns of the neighbors are fair, the applicant has the city’s zoning
  requirement and does not see a basis for rejecting this application.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that he is sure some of the commissioners have visited
  the site at least a couple of times and certainly consider the objections. In regards to the access
  issues for construction; this is something that is addressed with every project and is a practical
  issue for city staff to address and is not a basis for denial. In regards to the size, there have been
  other projects in the neighborhood that have been approved, some of which include, 7 Empty
  Saddle Road at 5,208 sq. ft., 48 Empty Saddle Road at 6,333 sq. ft. and a two-story home was
  approved a few months ago. In regards to Neighborhood Compatibility, the style and materials that
  are proposed for the home are not an issue, but expressed his concern with the scale and would
  feel better approving the second story if the size was reduced.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that properties are being purchased by new families and
  there should be consideration for the size of families moving into the neighborhoods. As long as
  the code is met and staff can support it, he does not see why this cannot be approved by the
  commission. He encourages applicants to work with their neighbors and concurs with the other
  commissioner’s statements.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that this project meets the code requirements except for Neighborhood
  Compatibility and stated that other projects have been rejected on mass, size and scale. He stated
  that this house is massed in a way that is inconsistent with the neighborhood. The second story
  massing is huge from the front and from the neighbor’s side. He does not dispute that they have
  met all the code requirements except for Neighborhood Compatibility.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that as a matter of value and character to the City,
  Neighborhood Compatibility is something she is sensitive to and would prefer to see the second
  story be lower and the mass reduced.

  CHAIR EDLER stated that the rear adds a lot of mass to the side view of the neighbor, but the
  proposal meets the code requirements. He would like to see more cooperation with the neighbors.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if the applicant would be willing to work with the neighbors
  to reduce the size of the building. Mr. Schneider stated that he is always willing to work with the
  community and ask his clients if they have any desire in reducing the size of the project.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if a proposal for a plate height reduced to 8’6” and roof pitch
  to 3:12 could be considered by the applicant. The applicant stated that the homeowners could
  consider this.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-200353 WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE
  PLATE HEIGHT BE REDUCED TO 8’6” AND THE ROOF PITCH BE CHANGED FROM
  4:12 TO 3:12.

  AYES: Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang
  NOES: Scott, Carman
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-200353, a request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination for one and
  two-story additions to be constructed along the front, side and rear yards of a single-story residence
  with a detached garage. A Minor Deviation to decrease the front yard area by less than 10% and
  for the encroachment of the proposed addition into the required front yard which does not project
  closer to the property line than the forwardmost building line and the added condition that the plate
  height be reduced to 8’6” and the roof pitch be changed from 4:12 to 3:12. There is a 20-day appeal
  period for this project whereby any member of the public may appeal this decision to the City
  Council.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  4
MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021
   B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-210045; ADDRESS: 3807 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: MR. PHILIP CHOI; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-210046) and Grading Permit (G-210047)
  for a new one-story residence with a basement.

  Planning Manager Naughton presented Planning Application No. PA-210045, 3807 Palos Verdes
  Drive North, which is Parcel 2 of Parcel Map No. 82074. On August 6, 2018, the Planning
  Commission approved PA-03-18 granting approval for Tentative Parcel Map No. 82074 consisting
  of a two-lot subdivision resulting in two RA-20 residentially zoned parcels. The site is currently
  developed with a swimming pool, tennis court and canopy and due to non-conforming setbacks,
  the lot coverage and use issues, these will be required to be removed prior to recording of the map.
  Due to Palos Verdes Drive North being a private street, the typical requirement for fire apparatus
  access, such as full turnaround at the north end of the street, do not exist. There is an existing
  intermediate turnaround at the southern end of the street near Palos Verdes Drive North public
  right-of-way. Due to this, there will be a 20’x20’ intermediate turnaround between Parcels 1 and 2
  with majority on Parcel 2, thus providing emergency access for the northern portion of the private
  drive of Palos Verdes Drive North. The intermediate turnaround will be required to be improved
  prior to construction of Parcel 2.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the applicant is proposing to construct a new one-story
  residence with a basement. An 800 sq. ft. horse keeping area has been identified in the
  southwestern portion of the rear yard. The one-story residence will contain approximately 4,300
  sq. ft. of living space on the main living level. The basement includes 800 sq. ft. of living area.
  There will be a 1,200 sq. ft. four car garage and 380 sq. ft. of storage on the east side of the garage.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
  Planning Application No. 210045, which includes a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  (NC-210046) and Grading Permit (G-210047), subject to the conditions contained in the staff
  report.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if the gate on the curb line at 3809 Palos Verdes Drive North is
  permitted. Planning Manager Naughton stated that there are several homes along the private drive
  that have the three-rail fence that are on the property line and go across the driveway, so it is not
  unusual for property owners to have the 42” high fencing in the front yard and is one exception in
  the H overlay zone. VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that the way that these gates have been installed
  make it difficult for fire equipment to turnaround since none of the driveways are useable.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked about 3809 exporting 138 cubic yards of cut and 3807 importing 240
  cubic yards of fill and asked if the 138 yards will be subtracted from the 240 yards. Planning
  Manager Naughton stated that there is a preliminary grading plan and this is what has been
  identified by the building engineers, but it is possible.

  CHAIR EDLER asked if there are other properties in the City where a driveway is used for a fire
  lane. Planning Manager Naughton stated that she cannot think of any, but staff thinks this is a good
  use of the driveway.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked if there will be a condition that no obstruction to that driveway be built.
  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the fire department requires that it be labeled “private
  driveway” and “fire lane”. There could be condition to added that no fencing is installed that could
  impede access to the driveway.

  Mike Chamberlain, Designer, stated that there is a condition that there be no parking in the
  driveway and that it be signed and noted, so he does not believe that this is an issue. He believes
  this would be a nice project for the area.

  Helena Lopez, 3745 Palos Verdes Drive North, stated that she is in favor of the project and looks
  forward to seeing a new home at that lot. Ms. Lopez stated that she believes that the existing
  turnaround are actually two parking spaces for the owner at the end of the street and requested
  that this be researched. Lastly, the residents of the street paid to have the street repaved and
  would like a condition added, that if there is any damage to the street that it be paid for at the
  applicant’s expense.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER, Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that, typically, when there are projects fronting the public right-of-way, there is a condition that the
  street be returned to its original condition and any damage and repairs be addressed.
  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER suggested taking photos. Planning Manager Naughton agreed
  and stated that a condition could be added that the applicant and neighbors work together to submit
  existing mutually agreed upon photos and agreement that they work out amongst themselves that
  any damage during construction be repaired to the pre-construction condition.

PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  5
MINUTES, MARCH 1, 2021
   COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if the neighbors are aware of the project. Planning Manager
  Naughton stated that it was noticed and notices were sent out to a 500’ radius. She was contacted
  by two neighbors, whom she sent copies of the plans and silhouette certification. No
  correspondence were received in favor or opposition of the project.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR stated that they seem to have a project that is presentable to the
  community and the neighbors. Seeing no opposition, he is able to support the project.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT stated that he would like to add the conditions, 1) that the driveway/fire lane
  not be blocked by any gate or parking along with the LA County Fire requirements; 2) that the
  applicant and neighbors enter into an agreement with the neighborhood to repair any damages to
  the street; and, 3) that the gate at 3809 Palos Verdes Drive North (same owner), which is in the
  public right-of-way be removed since it can be installed 25’ up the driveway and not impact his lot
  and it would also increase safety to provide more room for emergency equipment and would
  aesthetically improve the street.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER stated that in regards to VICE CHAIR SCOTT’s condition 2, that
  a stipulation be added to provide existing photos of the street.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Planning Manager Naughton stated
  that the City does not have access to a drone and would rely on photos taken at the street level
  and in addition, a walk could be arranged with the Community Development/Public Works Director
